title: Waze to beat the system: a real-world evaluation of crowdsourced enforcement alerts on driver speed
abstract: Objectives Crowdsourced navigation applications such as Waze allow users to report speed enforcement locations in real time, alerting nearby drivers to the presence of police or speed cameras. Despite the widespread adoption of these platforms, limited research has examined whether enforcement alerts influence the speed of individual vehicles at an active enforcement site. This study addresses that gap using a real-world, quasi-experimental pre–post design to assess the impact of crowdsourced enforcement alerts on vehicle speed across multiple road environments in Queensland, Australia. Methods Vehicle speeds were measured using a ProLaser 4 speed detection device at 33 sites spanning various speed zones (40–100 km/h) and multiple road types including arterial, residential, commercial, highway, mixed, and active school zone environments. At each site, speeds were recorded during a baseline period before an enforcement alert appeared on Waze, and during a matched post-alert period of equal duration. Results Analysis of 9052 speed observations across 33 sites found a statistically significant reduction in speed relative to the posted limit following the appearance of enforcement alerts on the navigation apps (Before: M = 1.23 km/h, SD = 8.34; After: M = -3.92 km/h, SD = 7.77). Conclusions These findings highlight that crowdsourced enforcement alerts are a contemporary mechanism of technology-facilitated punishment avoidance and while suppressing speed at the point of detection, may erode the perceived certainty of apprehension and embolden offending across the wider road network over time. The practical implications of this study suggest that road policing in a digitally connected environment may benefit from shorter, more geographically dispersed deployments, with the appearance of an enforcement alert leveraged as a trigger to reposition enforcement, acting as a force multiplier for a finite enforcement resource.
